disease_db.name: Apple___Apple_scab
disease_db.cause: Fungus Venturia inaequalis. Favorable conditions are cool, wet weather.
disease_db.cure: Use fungicides and resistant apple varieties. Prune and destroy infected leaves.

disease_db.name: Apple___Black_rot
disease_db.cause: Caused by the fungus Botryosphaeria obtusa.
disease_db.cure: Prune and remove infected areas. Apply fungicides during the growing season.

disease_db.name: Apple___Cedar_apple_rust
disease_db.cause: Fungus Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae. Requires junipers as an alternate host.
disease_db.cure: Remove nearby juniper hosts. Use resistant varieties and fungicides.

disease_db.cure: Maintain good cultural practices for optimal health.

chemical_pesticide.name: Mancozeb 75% WP / Difenoconazole 25% EC
chemical_pesticide.dosage: 2.0 - 2.5 g per liter of water (or 0.5 ml/L for Difenoconazole)

organic_alternative.name: Wettable Sulfur 80% WP or Liquid Copper Octanoate

Apple___Apple_scab.application_guide: Apply immediately at first appearance of olive-brown spots. Thoroughly coat upper and lower leaf surfaces. Repeat every 7-10 days during humid or rainy weather.
Apple___Apple_scab.safety_notes: Wear protective mask and gloves. Observe a 14-day Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI).

organic_alternative.name: Copper Soap Fungicide / Bordeaux Mixture 1%
organic_alternative.dosage: 10 g Copper Sulfate + 10 g Lime in 1L water

Apple___Black_rot.application_guide: Prune out dead twigs and mummified fruit first. Spray canopy completely during early morning.
Apple___Black_rot.safety_notes: Avoid spraying during peak blossom to protect pollinating bees.

organic_alternative.name: Sulfur Dust or Serenade Garden Disease Control (Bacillus subtilis)

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.application_guide: Begin sprays when pink flower buds appear and continue through petal fall at 7-10 day intervals.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.safety_notes: Do not enter treated orchards without protective gear within 24 hours.

organic_alternative.name: Potassium Bicarbonate or Cold-Pressed Neem Oil (1500 PPM)

Cherry___Powdery_mildew.application_guide: Spray early morning before sunlight turns intense. Coat both sides of tender new leaves.
Cherry___Powdery_mildew.safety_notes: Do not apply sulfur-based sprays within 30 days of oil sprays.

chemical_pesticide.name: Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC
chemical_pesticide.dosage: 1.0 ml per liter of water (200 ml per acre)

organic_alternative.name: Bio-fungicide Trichoderma viride / harzianum

Corn___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray_leaf_sp.application_guide: Spray at VT-R1 growth stage (tasseling/silking) if lesions appear on the third leaf below ear leaf or higher.
Corn___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray_leaf_sp.safety_notes: Do not apply within 30 days of maize harvest.

chemical_pesticide.name: Propiconazole 25% EC or Mancozeb 75% WP
chemical_pesticide.dosage: 1.0 ml/L for Propiconazole OR 2.5 g/L for Mancozeb

organic_alternative.name: Sulfur 80% WDG or Cold-Pressed Pure Neem Oil
organic_alternative.dosage: 2.5 g per liter of water (Sulfur) or 5 ml/L (Neem oil)

Corn___Common_rust.application_guide: Apply foliar spray when rust pustules cover >5% of upper canopy leaves. Ensure complete coverage of leaf whorls.
Corn___Common_rust.safety_notes: Wear protective eyewear and face shield during spraying.

organic_alternative.name: Bacillus amyloliquefaciens microbial bio-spray

Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.application_guide: Spray at first sign of cigar-shaped elliptical lesions, particularly during periods of high dew and moderate temperatures.
Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.safety_notes: Observe recommended buffer zones around water bodies.

organic_alternative.name: Bordeaux Mixture 1% or Copper Oxychloride 50% WP

Grape___Black_rot.application_guide: Apply from pre-bloom until 4-6 weeks after bloom to protect sensitive developing berries.
Grape___Black_rot.safety_notes: Allow 66 days PHI for Mancozeb in vineyards.

chemical_pesticide.name: Thiophanate-Methyl wound paste / Fosetyl-Aluminium foliar spray

organic_alternative.name: Trichoderma atroviride trunk paste
organic_alternative.dosage: Apply concentrated paste directly on pruning cuts

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).application_guide: Seal vine pruning cuts immediately after cutting. Foliar systemic sprays assist vine defense against vascular clogging.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).safety_notes: Sanitize pruning shears in 70% alcohol between vines.

chemical_pesticide.name: Carbendazim 50% WP or Copper Hydroxide 53.8% WG

organic_alternative.name: Copper Soap Fungicide

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.application_guide: Spray canopy thoroughly after rainfall. Ensure underside of leaves is drenched.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.safety_notes: Avoid spraying when temperatures exceed 32°C (90°F) to avoid leaf scorch.

chemical_pesticide.name: Imidacloprid 17.8% SL or Thiamethoxam 25% WG (Vector Control)
chemical_pesticide.dosage: 0.5 ml per liter of water (Imidacloprid) or 0.3 g/L (Thiamethoxam)

organic_alternative.name: High-Grade Horticultural Spray Oil (1.5%) + Neem Oil 3000 PPM
organic_alternative.dosage: 15 ml mineral oil + 4 ml neem oil per liter

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).application_guide: Target new flush leaves where psyllids feed and lay eggs. Prune out symptomatic yellow shoots. Apply zinc & nutritional foliar sprays to boost tree resilience.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).safety_notes: Do not spray while citrus trees are in full bloom to protect honeybees.

chemical_pesticide.name: Copper Oxychloride 50% WP + Streptocycline (Agri-Mycin)
chemical_pesticide.dosage: 2.0 g Copper + 0.6 g Streptocycline per 10 liters water

organic_alternative.name: Fixed Copper Hydroxide (low rate) or Bacillus subtilis

Peach___Bacterial_spot.application_guide: Apply from petal fall through cover sprays. Use low copper rates during leafed stages to avoid phytotoxicity.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.safety_notes: Avoid application in hot, sunny midday conditions.

chemical_pesticide.name: Copper Hydroxide 53.8% WG mixed with Mancozeb 75% WP
chemical_pesticide.dosage: 2.0 g Copper Hydroxide + 2.0 g Mancozeb per liter of water

organic_alternative.name: Bacillus amyloliquefaciens (Bio-fungicide) or Liquid Copper Octanoate

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.application_guide: Spray on a 7-day schedule when conditions are warm and wet. Avoid handling wet plants to prevent bacterial spread.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.safety_notes: Wash spray equipment thoroughly; keep out of child reach.

chemical_pesticide.name: Chlorothalonil 75% WP or Mancozeb 75% WP or Difenoconazole 25% EC
chemical_pesticide.dosage: 2.0 - 2.5 g per liter of water (or 0.5 ml/L Difenoconazole)

organic_alternative.name: Copper Oxychloride 50% WP or Trichoderma viride

Potato___Early_blight.application_guide: Apply at the first appearance of concentric brown ring spots on bottom leaves. Re-spray every 7-10 days.
Potato___Early_blight.safety_notes: Wear respirator during mixing. 7-day Pre-Harvest Interval.

chemical_pesticide.name: Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP (Systemic) or Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP

organic_alternative.name: Copper Hydroxide 77% WP or Bordeaux Mixture 1%

Potato___Late_blight.application_guide: URGENT INTERVENTION: Late blight can destroy a field in 4-7 days. Spray immediately across all foliage and stems; re-apply every 5-7 days under cool, foggy or rainy weather.
Potato___Late_blight.safety_notes: Rotate active ingredients to prevent pathogen resistance. Wear complete PPE.

chemical_pesticide.name: Penconazole 10% EC or Trifloxystrobin 25% + Tebuconazole 50% WG

organic_alternative.name: Potassium Bicarbonate (MilStop) or Diluted Milk Solution (40% milk / 60% water)

Squash___Powdery_mildew.application_guide: Spray white powdery patches promptly. Spray both upper and lower surface of giant squash leaves.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.safety_notes: Do not spray in midday sun to avoid leaf burn.

organic_alternative.name: Copper Soap or Bio-fungicide Bacillus subtilis

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.application_guide: Remove severely blighted old leaves before spraying. Apply to crowns and newly emerging runner leaves.

chemical_pesticide.name: Copper Hydroxide 53.8% WG + Streptocycline (Plant Bactericide)
chemical_pesticide.dosage: 2.0 g Copper Hydroxide + 0.1 g Streptocycline per liter water

organic_alternative.name: Liquid Copper Octanoate or Bacillus amyloliquefaciens

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.application_guide: Spray when plants are dry, covering flowers and young fruits. Repeat every 7 days in wet rainy spells.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.safety_notes: Wear waterproof gloves and face mask.

chemical_pesticide.name: Chlorothalonil 75% WP or Mancozeb 75% WP or Azoxystrobin 23% SC
chemical_pesticide.dosage: 2.0 g per liter of water (Chlorothalonil) or 1.0 ml/L (Azoxystrobin)

organic_alternative.name: Copper Oxychloride 50% WP or Organic Neem Oil (1500 PPM)

Tomato___Early_blight.application_guide: Prune out bottom 12 inches of infected leaves to increase air circulation, then spray remaining plant thoroughly.
Tomato___Early_blight.safety_notes: Re-entry interval: 24 hours. Wash hands after handling.

chemical_pesticide.name: Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP (Ridomil Gold) or Dimethomorph 50% WP
chemical_pesticide.dosage: 2.5 g per liter of water (Ridomil) or 1.0 g/L (Dimethomorph)

organic_alternative.name: Copper Hydroxide 53.8% WG or Bordeaux Mixture 1%

Tomato___Late_blight.application_guide: CRITICAL EMERGENCY: Apply immediately. Late blight moves rapidly through stems and fruit. Spray upper and lower leaves, stems, and flower trusses.
Tomato___Late_blight.safety_notes: Destroy heavily blighted vines by bagging; do not compost.

organic_alternative.name: Potassium Bicarbonate or Copper Soap Spray

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.application_guide: Ensure high ventilation and reduce humidity. Spray the pale yellow spots and velvety olive mold on lower leaf surfaces.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.safety_notes: Ventilate greenhouse/tunnel before and after spraying.

organic_alternative.name: Liquid Copper Fungicide or Serenade Bio-spray

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.application_guide: Spray from bottom upwards, thoroughly drenching both surface of leaves where tiny dark-rimmed spots start.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.safety_notes: Mulch soil surface to prevent soil splash during rain.

chemical_pesticide.name: Abamectin 1.9% EC or Spiromesifen 22.9% SC (Miticide)
chemical_pesticide.dosage: 0.75 ml per liter of water (Abamectin) or 1.0 ml/L (Spiromesifen)

organic_alternative.name: Cold-Pressed Neem Oil 3000 PPM or Insecticidal Potassium Soap
organic_alternative.dosage: 5.0 ml per liter of water (with a few drops of mild dish soap as emulsifier)

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.application_guide: High-pressure spray directed specifically at the UNDERSIDE of leaves where mites feed and spin webs. Apply in the evening.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.safety_notes: Wear respirator; do not spray during midday heat.

organic_alternative.name: Copper Hydroxide 53.8% WG

Tomato___Target_Spot.application_guide: Spray when circular brown target-like lesions are seen on foliage or green fruits. Ensure good air circulation.
Tomato___Target_Spot.safety_notes: Observe pre-harvest safety interval of 7 days.

chemical_pesticide.name: Diafenthiuron 50% WP or Acetamiprid 20% SP (Whitefly Vector Control)

organic_alternative.name: Yellow Sticky Traps + Cold-Pressed Neem Oil 3000 PPM
organic_alternative.dosage: 5.0 ml per liter of water sprayed on whitefly resting zones

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.application_guide: There is no direct cure for viral infections once inside the plant; control whitefly insect vectors immediately to stop transmission to adjacent crops.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.safety_notes: Remove and securely bag heavily stunted plants.

chemical_pesticide.name: Skim Milk Solution (20% concentration) or Trisodium Phosphate (TSP) tool sterilizer
chemical_pesticide.dosage: 200 ml milk per 800 ml water (Spray to inhibit viral transmission by contact)

organic_alternative.name: Soap solution tool wash + Neem spray for insect vectors
organic_alternative.dosage: Sterilize shears and hands in 10% TSP or milk before touching clean plants

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.application_guide: Viruses cannot be cured with standard fungicides. Immediately rogue out (remove & destroy) infected plants. Wash hands thoroughly with soap after handling.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.safety_notes: Do not compost infected plants. Wash smoker hands as tobacco can carry mosaic virus.

nutrients_lacking.deficiency_cause: Alternaria solani aggressively targets foliage with low potassium status. Potassium-deficient leaves accumulate soluble sugars and free amino acids that fungal hyphae readily consume.
nutrients_lacking.symptoms: Marginal leaf scorch, bronze flecking, accelerated bottom-leaf dieback.
nutrients_lacking.dosage: 4.0 - 5.0 g per liter of water (foliar spray)

nutrients_lacking.deficiency_cause: Fungal necrosis disrupts micronutrient uptake, leading to stunted leaf blade expansion and reduced plant phytoalexin defense.
nutrients_lacking.symptoms: Interveinal chlorosis, small leaves, reduced internode elongation.

Potato___Early_blight.nutrient_recovery_plan: Apply a high-potassium foliar feed combined with chelated zinc immediately after removing severely infected lower leaves. Avoid excessive nitrogen which promotes soft, vulnerable vegetative growth.
Potato___Early_blight.soil_advice: Ensure soil pH is between 5.5 - 6.5. Top-dress with well-rotted organic compost enriched with wood ash (rich in potassium).

nutrients_lacking.deficiency_cause: Phytophthora zoospores produce pectinases that dissolve the middle lamella. Insufficient calcium makes epidermal cell walls highly porous and unable to resist enzymatic digestion.
nutrients_lacking.symptoms: Blackened necrosis, water-soaked leaf margins, stem collapse.

nutrients_lacking.deficiency_cause: Extensive vascular breakdown caused by late blight blocks phloem translocation of magnesium, halting carbohydrate synthesis.
nutrients_lacking.symptoms: Rapid interveinal yellowing followed by dark necrotic lesions.

Potato___Late_blight.nutrient_recovery_plan: Foliar application of water-soluble Calcium Nitrate to reinforce cell wall strength in unaffected foliage. Rebalance soil nutrition once blight is chemically halted.
Potato___Late_blight.soil_advice: Avoid over-watering and poorly drained soils. Maintain balanced calcium-to-magnesium soil saturation.

nutrients_lacking.deficiency_cause: Alternaria solani thrives on stressed plants deficient in potassium. Plants redirect potassium to fruits, leaving vegetative leaves vulnerable to rapid necrotic spot development.
nutrients_lacking.symptoms: Yellow halos around target spots, curling leaf tips, premature defoliation.

nutrients_lacking.deficiency_cause: Nitrogen exhaustion during heavy fruiting stages weakens lower vegetative leaves, inviting Alternaria spores.
nutrients_lacking.symptoms: Pale green bottom foliage with concentric brown ring spots.

Tomato___Early_blight.nutrient_recovery_plan: Foliar feed with 0:52:34 (MKP) to supply both phosphorus and potassium directly to leaf stomata, bypassing stressed roots.
Tomato___Early_blight.soil_advice: Mulch the root zone with straw to prevent soil-splash pathogens and retain consistent root moisture.

nutrients_lacking.deficiency_cause: Phytophthora easily destroys soft tissues low in calcium. Calcium strengthens the structural matrix against oomycete mycelial growth.
nutrients_lacking.symptoms: Dark greasy water-soaked lesions on stems, petiole collapse, fruit rot.

nutrients_lacking.deficiency_cause: Infection disrupts ATP generation and energy transport needed for phytoalexin defense compounds.
nutrients_lacking.symptoms: Purpling of leaf veins followed by greasy wilt.

Tomato___Late_blight.nutrient_recovery_plan: After applying systemic fungicides (Ridomil Gold), spray Calcium Nitrate to fortify remaining healthy vines and fruit clusters.
Tomato___Late_blight.soil_advice: Ensure high aeration in soil. Avoid cold, saturated root zones.

nutrients_lacking.deficiency_cause: Xanthomonas bacteria invade through hydathodes and stomata. Low calcium creates fragile intercellular spaces that easily leak nutrients to bacteria.
nutrients_lacking.symptoms: Small greasy water-soaked specks turning brown with chlorotic borders.

nutrients_lacking.deficiency_cause: Boron deficiency inhibits phenolic defense synthesis, leaving tomato cuticle thin and prone to bacterial lesions.
nutrients_lacking.symptoms: Brittle stems, stunted leaf buds, deformed small fruit lesions.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.nutrient_recovery_plan: Foliar spray of Calcium + Boron combo (Cal-Bor) to rebuild cuticular wax and harden leaves against bacterial colonization.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.soil_advice: Maintain soil pH around 6.2 - 6.8. Avoid overhead splash irrigation.

nutrients_lacking.deficiency_cause: High leaf nitrogen combined with low calcium results in thin, succulent leaf layers easily penetrated by Venturia inaequalis ascospores.
nutrients_lacking.symptoms: Olive-brown velvety spots, puckered distorted leaves, scabby fruit.
nutrients_lacking.supplement: Foliar Calcium Chloride or Calcium Chelate

nutrients_lacking.deficiency_cause: Silicon polymerizes beneath the cuticle, forming a mechanical barrier against fungal appressoria penetration.
nutrients_lacking.symptoms: Soft foliage susceptible to fungal spore adhesion.

Apple___Apple_scab.nutrient_recovery_plan: Apply post-bloom calcium sprays bi-weekly. Supplement with potassium silicate to deposit hard silica armor on apple leaf surfaces.
Apple___Apple_scab.soil_advice: Apply dolomitic lime to acid soils in autumn to boost available calcium and magnesium.

nutrients_lacking.deficiency_cause: Puccinia rust pustules rupture epidermal cells, triggering intense transpiration and potassium leaching from foliage.
nutrients_lacking.symptoms: Golden/cinnamon powdery pustules, leaf edge drying, weak stalk strength.

nutrients_lacking.deficiency_cause: Rust infection draws massive amounts of plant carbohydrates and phosphate to sustain fungal sporulation.
nutrients_lacking.symptoms: Purplish red tint on lower leaves, slowed ear development.

Corn___Common_rust.nutrient_recovery_plan: Spray 0:0:50 Potassium Sulfate to arrest water loss and restore turgor pressure in infected maize whorls.
Corn___Common_rust.soil_advice: Side-dress maize with balanced NPK before tasseling; avoid excess nitrogen without matching potassium.

nutrients_lacking.deficiency_cause: Spider mites pierce individual plant cells and consume the chloroplasts, triggering intense bronzing and magnesium starvation.
nutrients_lacking.symptoms: Speckled stippled yellowing of leaves, webbing, bronze scorched foliage.

nutrients_lacking.deficiency_cause: Cellular sap draining restricts micronutrient uptake to terminal shoots.
nutrients_lacking.symptoms: Fine bleached stippling across upper canopy leaves.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.nutrient_recovery_plan: Foliar spray with Magnesium Sulfate + Chelated Micronutrient solution 24 hours after applying miticide/neem oil to stimulate chlorophyll regeneration.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.soil_advice: Ensure consistent soil moisture; drought-stressed plants produce higher nitrogen sap that attracts mite swarms.

Tomato___healthy.nutrient_recovery_plan: Crop nutrition is in optimal equilibrium. Maintain regular fertigation schedule with balanced NPK (19:19:19) and periodic compost tea.
Tomato___healthy.soil_advice: Keep soil organic matter >3% and mulch to sustain beneficial rhizosphere microorganisms.
